children.topic: HPD 500 · Paediatrics and Child Health II
children.note: Clinical paediatrics for the Kenyan hospital: neonatal emergencies, pneumonia, diarrhoea, malnutrition, malaria, HIV, TB, sickle cell, heart and kidney disease and childhood cancers, using the Basic Paediatric Protocols.

Clinical obstetrics and gynaecology: the major causes of maternal death in Kenya (haemorrhage, hypertension, sepsis, obstructed labour), medical disorders in pregnancy, early pregnancy problems, infertility and gynaecological cancers.
Applied community health: health systems, policy, financing, management, screening, outbreak response, HIV/TB/malaria and NCD programmes, occupational health, research and M&E.

children.note: Minimal change disease, usually steroid-sensitive.

children.note: Painless flank mass in a child aged 2–5 years that does not cross the midline; may have haematuria or hypertension.

children.note: Leukocoria (white pupillary reflex) or squint; RB1 gene on chromosome 13q14.

manas.q: What is the classic presenting sign of retinoblastoma?
